intro: Beneath your feet lies a floor once trodden in a palace courtyard. You are in the Great Palace Mosaic Museum, in İstanbul province, opened in 1953. This is the mosaic floor of the Byzantine Great Palace courtyard, kept where it was found and roofed over. And look at what it shows: not court life, but scenes of hunting, herding and animals.
history: In the late 1930s, excavations behind Sultanahmet uncovered a vast mosaic floor that once paved the colonnaded court of the Byzantine Great Palace. Rather than lifting it and carrying it away, they roofed it where it lay and opened it as a museum. It dates to the early Byzantine period, and surprisingly it shows not the life of the court but the countryside.
highlights: As you wander, take in the Mosaic floor as a whole, then look closer at the Hunting scenes. Walk along the Peristyle gallery, and don't miss the Elephant and lion panel.
facts: Did you know? More than a hundred human and animal figures have been counted across its scenes, and not one of them is religious or dynastic. The mosaic was never lifted: it is kept exactly where it was found, as the courtyard floor of the Byzantine palace. Instead of emperors or saints, hunters, herdsmen and animals describe life in the countryside.
outro: This brings our tour of the Great Palace Mosaic Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these colours stay bright for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
